label: Drawer width

description: The drawer's inside, front to back

label: Drawer clearance
description: How much smaller than the drawer the plate is, in total (both sides together)

name: print_bed
label: Print bed
description: The usable size of your printer's bed, its smaller side; the plate is split into pieces that fit it

name: style
label: Style
description: Light: a 3.6 mm floor with a window in every cell. Solid: a full 3.6 mm floor. Weighted: a 6.4 mm bottom with a pocket under every cell for a steel weight. Thin: the 4.75 mm frame only, no floor (no magnets, screws or clips)

name: magnet_holes
label: Magnet holes
description: 6.5 x 2.4 mm holes for 6 x 2 mm magnets in the four corners of every cell (not in the Thin style)

name: screw_holes
label: Screw holes
description: A countersunk M3 hole in the middle of every cell, to screw the plate to the drawer (Solid style only: the other styles have nothing to hold the screw there)

name: connector
label: Joints between pieces
description: Bowtie clips press into pockets underneath and hold neighbouring pieces together; None lets them just butt up against each other (the only choice in the Thin style, which has no floor)

name: show_drawer
label: Show drawer and sample bin
description: The drawer and one sample bin, for the picture. Switch off before exporting: then File > Export of the model as 3MF holds every piece and the clips in rows that fit the bed, and nothing else

name: connector_fit
label: Clip fit
description: Play between a clip and its pocket, on every side

title: Gridfinity baseplate
author: 3DCraft Jigs
description: A Gridfinity baseplate made to fill a drawer: give the drawer's inside and your print bed, and it fits as many 42 mm cells as it can, centred, with filler strips to the walls, split into pieces that each fit the bed. The pieces lock together with bowtie clips printed apart (or just butt together). Light, Solid, Weighted or Thin, with magnet holes and screw holes if you want. Any Gridfinity bin seats in it, including those of the Gridfinity bin Jig. Export: switch off Show drawer and sample bin, then File > Export the model as 3MF: every piece as a named object and the clips in rows that fit the bed, all flat, in the print orientation. Gridfinity is by Zack Freedman (MIT).
